THE IDEA

Learn the curve, one update at a time.

The model predicts ŷ = w₀ + w₁x + w₂x² + … + wₙxⁿ. Degree 1 is a straight line. Degree 2 includes x²; degree 3 adds x³. It is still linear regression in its coefficients, even when the curve is nonlinear in x.

Backpropagation follows the error backwards from ½(ŷ − y)² through the sum to every coefficient. The derivative for wᵢ is (ŷ − y)xⁱ. Each epoch averages those gradients over training points and updates wᵢ ← wᵢ − rate × gradient. There is no sigmoid, no hidden layer, and no closed-form solver.

Compare degree 1 and degree 2 on Parabola to see underfitting. Try a higher degree with noisy or sparse data to explore overfitting. Higher powers can learn slowly because polynomial features are correlated.

Test points never update the coefficients. RMSE measures error in y units. R² can be negative when predictions are worse than the test-set mean; it is undefined for constant targets. Small datasets may have no test set.

Drawing, importing, resampling, or changing model settings resets training. Changing the epoch target keeps learned coefficients. The curve may predict outside −1 to 1; the plot clips it at its edges, while numeric inspection shows the full output. Changing pages or refreshing starts a new experiment.

YOUR DATA

Bring your own points.

Use two columns, x,y, with an optional header. Both values must be between −1 and 1. Import 2–1,000 rows. Importing replaces the data and resets training.
